tasks.analysis: Mass extinctions have periodically reshaped the diversity of life on Earth, representing significant biological and ecological shifts. The most famous event, the Cretaceous-Paleogene extinction, occurred approximately 66 million years ago and led to the demise of the dinosaurs. Large-scale losses of species are often caused by catastrophic events such as volcanic eruptions, asteroid impacts, and climate change. The resulting damage to biodiversity disrupts ecosystems and alters evolutionary trajectories. Studying past extinctions provides insights into the resilience and adaptability of life, helping scientists predict and mitigate future biodiversity loss. 大规模灭绝周期性地重塑了地球生命的多样性，标志着重大的生物与生态转变。最著名的是白垩纪 — 古近纪灭绝事件，发生在约 6600 万年前，导致恐龙消亡。大规模物种丧失通常由火山爆发、小行星撞击、气候变化等灾难事件引发。由此造成的生物多样性破坏会扰乱生态系统、改变进化轨迹。研究过去的灭绝事件有助于理解生命的韧性与适应能力，帮助科学家预测并减少未来生物多样性损失。
